column1: 3 · THE RULES THAT KEEP IT SAFE

column2: Cost floor — no card may be priced below its own cost per credit, measured against the ceiling ($0.0035, set by Redesign My Room).
column3: Breaking it makes the worst case unbounded. Shop My Room broke it at 12 credits ($0.0067/cr, nearly 2x a render); fixed at 25.

column2: Arbitrage gate — one subscription month must be WORSE credits-per-dollar than Project. Currently 20.4 vs 23.3.
column3: If a single month were the cheapest credits on the page, pack buyers would subscribe, burn it and cancel. Re-check on EVERY price change.

column2: Ladder — credits per dollar must rise with price: 10.3 → 23.3 → 26.1.
column3: Starter is deliberately the worst value; if it were generous nobody would climb to Project.

column2: Guidance, not limits — the page may say what people typically do, never what they are allowed to do.
column3: No 'up to N rooms'. Nothing counts rooms; credits are the only limit. A limit the code does not enforce is a false promise and a support ticket.
The moment it promises '300 included' it becomes a per-tool allowance: 19 tools x 4 plans = 76 numbers to maintain forever.

column2: Licence boundary is BUSINESS USE — never whose home it is. Pay-once packs grant personal, non-commercial use of ANY home (your own, a family member's, a friend's, a flat you're renovating). The subscription grants use in the course of business — client work, staging listings, rentals — and output made while subscribed stays usable after cancelling.
column3: The obvious-looking rule ('your own home') is factually wrong: people buy a pack for a parent's flat or a place they are flipping. Owner caught this 2026-09-05. The licence is also UNENFORCEABLE — treat it as a term, not a fence; the real wall is the arithmetic plus the watermark. You can only grant rights you hold: Google's Gemini API terms cap what you may license, and third-party retailer content inside Shop My Room is not yours to license at all — the grant covers the GENERATED DESIGN only.
